_about: SAN-1321 — expected public.mastra_* schema for the MDE production feature contract, plus the @mastra/core + @mastra/pg pairing that produces it.
_derivation: The expectedTables list is the public.mastra_* set MDE's runtime and production feature contract require. It is the 32 tables verified against production project zkwcbyxiwklihegjhuql on 2026-09-18, plus mastra_workflow_run_owners and mastra_memory_run_fences, which @mastra/core@1.81.0 and @mastra/pg@1.34.0 newly require and which supabase/migrations/20261104031855_mastra_181_run_ownership.sql adds (SAN-1626). adapterVersion/coreVersion record the certified pairing: @mastra/pg@1.34.0 with @mastra/core@1.81.0. A fresh `npm run mastra:init` with that adapter creates 39 tables — the 34 below plus the 5 adapterInitExtraTables the upgraded adapter still creates. That is down from 43: the six mastra_knowledge_* tables are no longer created by @mastra/pg@1.34.0 and remain listed in adapterInitExtraTables only so an older environment is still described correctly. Runtime proof (SAN-1626, disposable PostgreSQL 17): with the previous 32-table footprint, `Run._start` fails 42P01 on mastra_workflow_run_owners, and with a keyless table it fails 42P10; after this migration a suspended workflow run persists and resumes across a cold start, writes mastra_workflow_snapshot and mastra_workflow_run_owners, and leaves mastra_memory_run_fences empty. The migration is therefore required, not optional.
_why: src/mastra/lib/storage.ts runs PostgresStore with disableInit: true, so nothing self-heals at runtime. A fresh environment provisioned with a mis-paired adapter would silently miss most of this schema. This file is the contract; scripts/check-mastra-schema-contract.mjs reports drift between it and the installed packages, and scripts/verify-mastra-schema-init.mjs fails when a real database provisions a mastra_* table this contract has not classified as required or optional.
_maintenance: When @mastra/core / @mastra/pg are upgraded, run `npm run mastra:init` against a scratch Postgres, diff the resulting public.mastra_* set against expectedTables plus adapterInitExtraTables, and classify every difference: prove whether the upgraded runtime reads/writes it on a normal agent, memory, or workflow path. If it does and production lacks it, a production-safe migration is a prerequisite — do not extend expectedTables merely to make the checker pass. An UNCLASSIFIED table now fails verification, which is deliberate: the 1.81 upgrade added two required tables that the previous contract did not classify, so CI passed while production would have failed. Update adapterVersion/coreVersion (and the table lists only when the required or created set genuinely changes) in one commit.
